TITLE: Distributed Reasoning in Unified Models for Image Editing
PROPOSAL: We design a set of experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of distributed reasoning between understanding and generation modules in a unified model for image editing. Specifically, we implement a new architecture, "SplitGen", which divides the responsibility of processing semantic conditions between a multimodal understanding module and a specialized image editing module, featuring iterative refinement and intermediate reasoning. This is tested on the COCO-Ed and LV Glove datasets, benchmarked against state-of-the-art proprietary models and against the current paradigm of integrated understanding and generation.
CONTROLS: BAGEL, Step1X-Edit, baseline unified models (Show-o, MetaQuery)
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant performance improvement on both datasets with the SplitGen architecture, along with intermediate reasoning modules, but at the cost of increased computational complexity. The results could fail if we do not address potential multi-modality misalignment issues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Multimodal Reasoning with Controlled Generation
PROPOSAL: To better support intermediate reasoning and refine the input to the generation module, we introduce an experiment where a modal-dynamic graph neural network (MDGNN) acts as a mediator between the understanding and generation modules. This MDGNN maps the semantic conditions from the understanding module onto a structured graph representation suitable for controlled generation by the image editing module. We test this on the COCO-Ed and LV Glove datasets using the SplitGen architecture.
CONTROLS: SplitGen without MDGNN, baseline unified models (Show-o, MetaQuery)
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that the MDGNN-based mediator will better enable controlled generation and overall accuracy in image editing tasks, outperforming the baseline unified models and improving upon the SplitGen architecture. However, potential performance degradation in tasks requiring highly dynamic graph structures might hinder the overall gain.

TITLE: Training Data Augmentation for Improved Instruction Understanding
PROPOSAL: We design an experiment to improve the understanding module's ability to comprehend complex instructions with training data augmentation. Specifically, we utilize data manipulation from CommonGen and COCO-E, which generates a diverse set of visually consistent yet semantically different renderings of the same input image for each instruction, as well as generate counterfactual explanations and additional intermediate images for counterfactual data mainstreams.

TITLE: Evaluating Integrated Understanding and Generation Paradigms
PROPOSAL: We design a set of comprehensive experiments to benchmark the state-of-the-art proprietary models (GPT-4o-Image) against our proposed unified models and the current paradigm of integrated understanding and generation. Specifically, we evaluate performance on a suite of image editing tasks, including COCO-Ed, COCO-Cars, LV Glove, and Flickr Material, and analyze the impact of our proposed architectures on model performance and computational efficiency.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art proprietary models (GPT-4o-Image), integrated understanding and generation models (Show-o, MetaQuery), baseline unified models (SplitGen, Modified SplitGen)
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant performance improvement in unified models over integrated understanding and generation models, especially on complex tasks that require intermediate reasoning, and that our modified SplitGen will outperform the baseline unified models in computational efficiency.

TITLE: Transfer Learning between Text-to-Image and Image Editing Tasks
PROPOSAL: We investigate the transferability of pre-trained text-to-image models to image editing tasks and explore whether fine-tuning on image editing datasets can improve performance. Specifically, we pre-train a Qwen2.5-VL-7B model on COCO-E and train it on COCO-Ed, LV Glove, and Flickr Material to evaluate performance on each task and analyze the impact of transfer learning on image editing performance.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art pre-trained text-to-image models (Show-o, MetaQuery), fine-tuned on image editing datasets
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant performance improvement in image editing tasks through transfer learning, especially when fine-tuning on COCO-Ed, and that this transferability can be effectively leveraged to create more robust and accurate image editing models. However, we also anticipate potential transfer oversights as some features may not be transferable.

TITLE: Model-Based Interpretability for Instruction-Guided Image Editing
PROPOSAL: We design and evaluate a model-based approach for interpretability in instruction-guided image editing models. This involves identifying and visualizing the key components and steps in the decision-making process that lead to the generated image, providing insights into the model's performance, and also attributing success or failure to specific components or interactions within the model pipeline.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art models and architectures (Modified SplitGen, Qwen2.5-VL-7B)
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to gain valuable insights into the decision-making process of image editing models and attribute failures to specific model components or interactions, which can inform model design, training, and optimization for improved performance.

PROPOSAL: We create a comprehensive benchmarking framework and set of evaluation metrics to assess the performance of unified image editing models, including evaluation of distributed reasoning, controlled generation, instruction understanding, and overall image editing quality. This will enable systematic comparison and improvement of existing and future models.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art unified image editing models (Modified SplitGen, Qwen2.5-VL-7B)

TITLE: Refining the Semantic Encoder with Interpretable Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of refining the semantic encoder with an interpretable reasoning module, using a custom-design attention mechanism that captures complex relationships between user instructions and image semantics. Evaluate this approach on UniWorld-V1 with the COCO-Edits benchmark, comparing the performance against the standard semantic encoder and recent integrative models like BAGEL and Step1X-Edit.
CONTROLS: Compare against UniWorld-V1 (standard semantic encoder), BAGEL, Step1X-Edit, and GPT-4o-Image (proprietary model baseline)
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will improve performance for complex edits, particularly those requiring nuanced understanding of object relationships and scene context. However, it may not address edit accuracy for very short instructions, and could introduce additional latency due to the additional reasoning step.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Coupled Understanding and Generation in Compact Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate whether a more balanced division of responsibilities between understanding and generation can improve image editing precision in compact models. Specifically, design a hierarchical model where the understanding module generates a coarse plan, which is then refined by the generation module through iterative rendering and refinement. Implement this coupled understanding and generation architecture on the ResNet-Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone using the COCO-Edits benchmark. Evaluate the model against state-of-the-art compilers like BAGEL and proprietary models like GPT-4o-Image.
CONTROLS: Compare against BAGEL, GPT-4o-Image, and the original single-stage ResNet-Qwen2.5-VL-7B model
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should improve edit precision for compact models by leveraging their ability to reason about inferred target images. However, it may come at the cost of slower generation times due to iterative refinement, and require larger evaluation datasets to ensure robustness.
